## Status: Draft
## Authors: [Platform Architecture Team]
## Date: 2026-03-31

---

## 1. Motivation

Our e-commerce platform currently runs as a single Django monolith serving all six core domains: catalog, orders, payments, user accounts, notifications, and inventory. While this architecture served us well during early growth, we have reached inflection points across multiple operational dimensions that necessitate decomposition.

### 1.1 Deploy Velocity Bottleneck
The current end-to-end deploy pipeline takes 45 minutes. With 200 engineers across 8 teams committing to a shared trunk, the deploy queue creates a 3-5 hour feedback loop from merge to production. Coupled modules mean that a change to the notification template rendering engine requires a full regression suite covering payments and inventory — domains with zero functional overlap.

### 1.2 Blast Radius of Failures
In Q4 2025, a memory leak in the catalog search indexer caused OOM kills that took down the entire platform, including payments processing. Post-incident analysis showed that 73% of our P1 incidents in the past 12 months had blast radii extending beyond the originating domain due to shared process boundaries.

### 1.3 Scaling Asymmetry
Catalog read traffic follows diurnal patterns with 10x peaks during flash sales, while payment processing is relatively steady. The monolith forces uniform scaling: we provision for peak catalog load, resulting in 4x over-provisioning of payment processing capacity, costing approximately $2.1M/year in excess compute.

### 1.4 Team Autonomy
Domain boundaries in the codebase do not enforce isolation. Teams routinely reach across module boundaries through direct database queries, shared ORM models, and in-process function calls. This creates implicit coupling that surfaces as merge conflicts (avg 12/week cross-team), broken contracts, and coordination overhead estimated at 15-20% of engineering time.

### 1.5 Technology Lock-in
All domains are constrained to Django 4.2/Python 3.11/PostgreSQL 15. The ML team needs to deploy real-time recommendation models that require GPU inference and would benefit from a Go or Rust serving layer. The notifications team wants to adopt an event-driven architecture with Kafka, but the synchronous request-response pattern of the monolith makes this impractical without architectural changes.

---

## 2. Goals
- Independent deployability per domain service (target: <10 min deploy per service)
- Fault isolation: failures in one domain do not cascade to others
- Independent scaling per domain based on actual traffic patterns
- Team autonomy: each team owns their service, schema, and deploy pipeline
- Incremental migration: no big-bang cutover; strangler fig pattern

## 3. Non-Goals
- Rewriting business logic (lift-and-shift, then optimize)
- Migrating to a different cloud provider
- Adopting Kubernetes (already on K8s)
- Changing the customer-facing API contract
